question: Protein digesting enzyme pepsin is secreted in the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**stomach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pepsin** is a proteolytic enzyme that is secreted by the **chief cells** in the stomach lining.
 
• The secretion is initially in the form of an inactive precursor called **pepsinogen**.
 
• Pepsinogen is converted to active pepsin in the acidic environment of the stomach, primarily due to the action of **hydrochloric acid (HCl)**.
 
• Pepsin plays a crucial role in the digestion of proteins, breaking them down into smaller peptides.
 
• The pH level in the stomach, which ranges from 1.5 to 3.5, is optimal for pepsin activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Cells:**

 
 
• These are cells in the stomach lining that secrete pepsinogen and gastric lipase.
 
• Chief cells are also known as zymogenic cells.
 
 
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl):**
 
 
• Produced by parietal cells in the stomach lining.
 
• Creates an acidic environment, which is necessary for the conversion of pepsinogen to pepsin.
 
 
 
• **Gastric Mucosa:**
 
 
• The mucous membrane layer of the stomach, which contains the glands and the gastric pits.
 
• Responsible for the secretion of gastric juices, including pepsinogen and HCl.
 
 
 
• **Protein Digestion:**
 
 
• Starts in the stomach with the action of pepsin.
 
• Continues in the small intestine with the help of other proteolytic enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin.
